institutionName: UiT The Arctic University of Norway

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Given that I had already been on an exchange in Europe (Milan) on my Bachelor's, and that my first choice of going to Asia was rejected, I wanted something new, different, and "exotic." This is where I saw a great match with the Arctic

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The place I lived in and the roomies I had played a crucial role in making the experience great! I was not impressed by the university level

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Relatively easy - Yet, the I was unimpressed by the help I got from a specific contact person from UiT (Mustta). I heard from several other students that this person had not cooperated very well and not answered the questions we forwarded. Ultimately, this led to me feeling limited in my choice of courses, because this person made it sound like I could not choose other courses - which was not true.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: ESN intro days

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
I was recommended by a friend to create a post in the Facebook group called: Til Leie/Ønskes Leid Tromsø

The first message I got ended up being the right match.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Tromsø island is surprisingly big, but you will easily manage to get around. Just beware that buses don't run regularly between 01:00 and 05:00, if not at all.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Samskipnaden, private, etc. There are surprisingly many good options.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very poor help from this specific ESN coordinator, Mussta. Did not do a good job at all.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
I don't recall the
details...You
're first accepted by the host university. Then you choose the courses you would like to attend. This is where I had many problems, and got very little help from Mussta, which made the whole registration process a mess. This ultimately led to not change my OLA, as I knew that it would be another round of mess, if I had to change it. Finally, once courses are apporved and OLA is signed, you are good.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: ESN coordinator via email - very bad.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not very good. To UiT's defence, the university in Tromsø is not ideal for an economist student - on the other hand, you get the opportunity to enroll in classes you normally wouldn't have, giving you new perspectives, which can benefit you as an economist.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be open to other classes than specifically those related to your studies. I ended up having three courses on Arctic Norway, stretching from culture, to history, to politics. Although I was not impressed by the workload or level, I still learned surprisingly much in each.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Arctic Norway - Aspects of (1) Culture, (2) History, (3) Politics, international relations and governance. These were the three courses I had, all BA level. Not impressed by the level nor the structure, yet I still managed to gain knowledge I didn't have before.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Unstructured, very limited workload, no one answer but more reflective answers allowed.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Arctic Norway - Aspects of (1) Culture, (2) History, (3) Politics, international relations and governance

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: If you are interested in the Arctic, I can recommend the history and politics course. But I would also look into other courses that may cover the Arctic in more depth at a higher level.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
First times shopping in the supermarket, you are surprised by the
prices...but
you gradually adjust your purchasing behaviour and look for discounts. I was told that alcohol is expensive, but was still surprised to experience it myself. Beware that supermarkets stop selling "light" alcohol after 18:00 in the evening on weekdays and 17:00 on saturdays, and I think it's the same for strong alcohol in Vinmonopolet (Norwegian liquor stores). Supermarkets are closed on Sundays.

Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot of different activities - football, diving, paddling, ...

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Kayaking + football

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Nature is veeery accessible near Tromsø - you can literally take a bus to the spot you are hiking or skitouring/randonee from. Most of the peaks you see and are interested in summitting, you can access. Of course, always check with locals, maps, etc. before for your own and others' safety. 

If you are up for cabin trips, you should get hold of a DNT key. This is the "master key" to all nearby DNT cabins in the nature. Remember to clean up after yourself and pay for your stay - it is all about trust. 

Other activities include going to Tromsø Badet, Pust sauna, Telegrafbukta to swim during summer (or winter if you dare), and Tromsø city.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Participate in the first ESN activities and trips, participate in sports, etc.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Trust society

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Go for the adventure
2) Take advantage of free waffles on Fridays
3) Beware of the darkness that will hit you in November if you go in the autumn semester

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: To cope with the darkness, you can borrow artificial sunlight lamps that will do the trick to keep you energised

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Access to nature and roommates - I was able to combine the two, by accessing nature on skis with my roommates, experiencing northern lights as we ascended a peak...magical

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I had very little uni during my stay, therefore it was actually the hardest to accept that I didn't have much to do, and be creative with my time in the High North.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
